newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-RAFTER BLANKS OUT BLANCO ON WAY TO SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RAFTER BLANKS OUT BLANCO ON WAY TO SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Patrick Rafter became the first Australian to reach the French Open men's semifinals in 20 years when he brought Galo Blanco's unlikely run in the French Open to a halt in the quarter-finals on Wednesday.
Having swept aside the 20-year-old Spaniard, ranked 111 in the world, 6-3 7-6 6-3 in front of a sparse Centre Court audience, Rafter's presence in the semifinals is itself unexpected.

Ranked 25th in the world, Rafter has but a single career title to his credit and had previously never advanced past the fourth round at Roland Garros, going out in the first round on his last two appearances in Paris.

"It's a dream for me," he said after avenging two earlier home court losses to Spaniards in Sydney and the Australian Open and becoming the first Australian to reach the men's singles last four here since Phil Dent in 1977.
"I knew I had to play my game because I was playing a clay-court specialist.
"I don't know, maybe this is my best surface, but three weeks ago I wasn't sure if I would come here at all. Now I'm glad I did."
Blanco, one of only two Spaniards to survive the first week at Roland Garros, had never before made it past the opening round of a grand slam tournament.
On Wednesday he appeared confounded by Rafter's attacking style.
"I didn't play as well as I would have liked to but I'm still happy with my tournament. It was all very unexpected," Blanco said.
Both players had most of the major hurdles in their quarter of the draw cleared from their path as the seeds tumbled out of their way in early-round losses.
Rafter reached his first grand slam semifinal having met just one player ranked higher than him, sixth-seeded reigning Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek of the Netherlands.
Rafter awaited the result of the day's other quarter-final between former champion Sergi Bruguera of Spain and unseeded Moroccan Hicham Arazi to know who is next opponent would be.
"I played Bruguera twice in Gstaad and Rome and had my butt kicked both times," Rafter said. "But Arazi might win, he's been playing some very flashy tennis.
"I've got nothing to lose but I have to stick to my game and play attacking tennis if I want to win."

The other semifinal pairing was decided on Tuesday. It pits Belgian qualifier Filip Dewulf, ranked 122 in the world, against Brazil's Gustavo Kuerten, who booked his place in the last four with a five-set win over defending champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov.
